title: Cloud Resilience & Distributed Fault Tolerance
summary: Architecting backend systems that withstand network drops, node crashes, and unexpected traffic surges.
keyPrinciples: Assume failure will happen: networks partition, disks fail, dependencies time out.
Fail fast with timeouts: never let a request wait indefinitely for a downstream dependency.
Graceful degradation: serve cached or partial data when non-critical services go offline.

rules.title: Apply Exponential Backoff with Jitter to Network Retries
rules.description: Retrying failed requests at fixed intervals causes all clients to retry simultaneously, hitting the recovering server with synchronized traffic waves (thundering herd).

badExample.explanation: Synchronized retries hammer the recovering service and knock it back offline.

goodExample.explanation: Randomizes retry timing, spreading load evenly across the recovery timeline.

productionChecklist: Strict timeouts defined on all external HTTP, gRPC, and database clients.
Circuit breakers (Resilience4j / Opossum) configured around fragile third-party APIs.
Health probes distinguish between `/healthz/live` (process alive) and `/healthz/ready` (ready for traffic).
Chaos engineering drills executed regularly in staging environments.
